summary: Verified bug fix: TournamentBasicsPanel now resolves parent Division when host_body_id is a DIST-* code, so Inter-District tournaments correctly populate district checkboxes on 'Add Pool'. Tested with two tournaments (DIST-ALIR-IND hosted 'Gwalior Division Inter-District Championship' and DIV-IND hosted 'Bhopal Division Inter-District Championship') plus an Inter_Divisional regression tournament.

issues: React hydration warning: <span> inside <option> at line 488 (visual-edit instrumentation wraps ground name option text). Non-blocking, but produces a console error on every Basics render. Consider excluding <option> children from the visual-edit span wrapper.

critical_code_review_comments: TournamentBasicsPanel.jsx line 76: when host_body_id is missing on an Inter_District tournament, bodies is cleared to []. UI already surfaces the Note ('this Inter-District tournament has no host Division set') at line 302, so behaviour is fine — flagging as intentional.

The extra /api/bodies/{host} lookup runs on every host_body_id change; consider memoising the parent-Division resolution or using a single backend endpoint that returns sibling districts by host body id to avoid double round-trip.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Bug fix for Inter-District pool step district population confirmed working via Playwright. DIST-* hosts now correctly resolve to parent Division and list all 8 sibling districts. DIV-* hosts continue to work directly. Inter_Divisional regression path shows 10 MPCA Divisions unchanged. Existing pool headers correctly render district names (bodyByCode lookup works after the fetch resolves).
rca_of_the_issue: Original bug: /api/bodies query used raw host_body_id as parent_code. When host_body_id was DIST-ALIR-IND, the query 'body_type=District&parent_code=DIST-ALIR-IND' returned empty (Districts have no District children). Fix in useEffect at lines 64-95: if host starts with 'DIST-', fetch /api/bodies/{host} first, use its parent_code (a DIV-* code) as the query parent. Verified end-to-end in UI.
